Macrons

Theme

Latin word

stips

stips, stipis f.

noun, third declension

a small coin given; alms; a small coin, an alms

In this lexicon

  • alms

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Vit. Beat. 25.1: quī manum ad stipem porrigunt, those who hold out their hand for alms; Suet. Aug. 91.2: stipem … ēmendīcābat ā populō; M-O s.v. charity: contribution or donation, alms

  • tip

    also used · classical · Traupman

Examples

  • In Sublicium pontem mē trānsfer et inter egentēs abjice: nōn ideō tamen mē dēspiciam quod in illōrum numerō cōnsēderō quī manum ad stipem porrigunt.

    Put me on the Sublician bridge and throw me among the needy: I shall not despise myself for sitting among those who hold out their hand for alms.Sen. Vit. Beat. 25.1

    In the entry for alms

  • Ex nocturnō vīsū etiam stipem quotannīs diē certō ēmendīcābat ā populō cavam manum assēs porrigentibus praebēns.

    Because of a dream he even begged alms from the people every year on a fixed day, holding out his cupped hand to those who offered him coins.Suet. Aug. 91.2

    In the entry for alms

  • Tē autem faciente eleēmosynam, nesciat sinistra tua quid faciat dextera tua

    But when you give alms, let not your left hand know what your right hand is doingVulg. Mt. 6.3
